# Hilde

> Hilde is a small, strict systems language with linear types that compiles to C. Modules are a body
> file .hiq and an interface file .hih; the command is hilde. A value that holds a resource is used
> exactly once, every case is handled, and there is no operator precedence: an operator takes two
> operands, and only +, *, and, or chain with themselves.

## Reserved words

These words are never names; the compiler refuses one with H0008 and suggests a free name (skip gives
skipCount, is gives holds):

and, as, body, borrow, case, constant, do, else, end, ensures, false, for, from, function, generic, if,
import, instance, invariant, is, let, method, module, nil, not, of, or, pragma, raise, raises, record,
requires, return, sizeof, skip, then, to, true, type, typeclass, union, var, when, while, and the type
words Free, Linear, Region, Type and Span.

## Docs

- [Syntax](docs/syntax.en.md): every form of the language, section 1 lists the reserved words
- [Errors](docs/errors.en.md): every error code with its message, an example that fails and the correct form
- [Traps](docs/hilde-traps.md): the mistakes met in writing Hilde, with the wrong and the right code
- [Learning Hilde](docs/learning-hilde.md): a guide from the first programme on

## Commands

- hilde compile: compile modules to C or a binary; hilde build is the same command
- hilde build --target=wasm: a module for wasm32-wasi, zig or clang found by hilde; the targets are
  linux, openbsd, freebsd, darwin and wasm, and every interface of the standard library names its
  own with pragma Targets
- hilde test: build and run the tests of test files; --target=wasm runs them in wasmtime
- hilde check: parse, type and check modules without writing C
- hilde modules: every module with its files and what it exports, --json for one JSON array
- hilde fmt: write sources in their one form
